title: Completed scalar extension commutes coherently with compatible coefficient lines
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a scheme $X$, and a chain $E_0\subseteq E_1\subseteq E_2$ of finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, allowing repeated fields. For $i=0,1,2$ let $\mathcal O_i$ be the valuation ring, $\pi_i$ a uniformizer, and $R_i=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{i,X}$ the completed coefficient sheaf on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived completeness [def-weil-derived-complete]. For $i\leq j$, let $B_{ji}K=K\otimes^L_{R_i}R_j$ be ordinary derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], let $C_{ji}$ be the strict quotient-tower integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Explicitly, set $A_{i,n}=\mathcal O_i/\pi_i^n$ for $n\geq1$, and let $\rho_{ji,n}:R_i\to(A_{j,n})_X$ be the projection $R_i\to(A_{i,n})_X$ followed by the same-index quotient map induced by $\mathcal O_i\subseteq\mathcal O_j$. For a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex], put $Q_{ji,n}=\operatorname{Res}^{j}_n(P\otimes_{R_i}(A_{j,n})_X)$, where $\operatorname{Res}^{j}_n$ is restriction along $R_j\to(A_{j,n})_X$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Then $C_{ji}K$ is the specified complex
$$\operatorname{Cone}\left(1-s:\prod_{n\geq1}Q_{ji,n}\longrightarrow\prod_{n\geq1}Q_{ji,n}\right)[-1],\qquad s((q_n)_n)=(t_n(q_{n+1}))_n,$$
with termwise products and transitions $t_n$ induced by the quotient maps. Use its specified natural completion comparison $\chi_{ji}:B_{ji}\to C_{ji}$ [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison].

Let $L_i$ be a locally free rank-one $R_i$-module sheaf (locally isomorphic to $R_i$). Suppose given isomorphisms $b_{ji}:L_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\xrightarrow{\sim}L_j$ for $i\leq j$, with $b_{ii}$ the multiplication map and $b_{20}=b_{21}\circ(b_{10}\otimes1)$ under tensor associativity. Write $L_i^{[0]}=R_i$, $L_i^{[m]}=L_i^{\otimes m}$ for $m>0$, and $L_i^{[m]}=\mathcal Hom_{R_i}(L_i^{[-m]},R_i)$ for $m<0$, using [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Set $T_{i,m}K=K\otimes^L_{R_i}L_i^{[m]}$. The evaluation isomorphisms give $\epsilon_{i,m}:T_{i,-m}T_{i,m}\xrightarrow{\sim}1$.

For every integer $m$, the ordinary scalar comparisons induced from $b_{ji}$, its tensor powers and its sheaf-dual maps give natural isomorphisms $\bar\beta_{ji,m}:B_{ji}T_{i,m}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{j,m}B_{ji}$. Each $T_{i,m}$ preserves derived completeness. On complete inputs, the conjugated maps
$$\beta_{ji,m,K}=T_{j,m}(\chi_{ji,K})\circ\bar\beta_{ji,m,K}\circ\chi_{ji,T_{i,m}K}^{-1}$$
are natural isomorphisms $C_{ji}T_{i,m}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{j,m}C_{ji}$. Let $a_K:C_{21}C_{10}K\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{20}K$ be ordinary tensor associativity transported by these specified $\chi$ maps. They satisfy
$$T_{2,m}(a_K)\circ\beta_{21,m,C_{10}K}\circ C_{21}(\beta_{10,m,K})=\beta_{20,m,K}\circ a_{T_{0,m}K},$$
and
$$\epsilon_{j,m,C_{ji}K}\circ T_{j,-m}(\beta_{ji,m,K})\circ\beta_{ji,-m,T_{i,m}K}=C_{ji}(\epsilon_{i,m,K}).$$
For a repeated field the comparison is the one induced by the tensor unitor and the natural completeness map $K\to C_{ii}K$, rather than a strict equality $C_{ii}=1$. These are the comparisons for the prescribed quotient-tower completion: on a K-flat representative with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex], followed by each finite quotient projection, the ordinary map is $(x\otimes l)\otimes s\mapsto(x\otimes s)\otimes b_{ji,m}(l\otimes1)$. The maps $\chi$ in this conjugation are the quotient maps into the strict completion cone with zero shifted-product component; no chain-level inverse to $\chi$ is asserted. Here $b_{ji,m}$ is the signed-power extension of $b_{ji}$, so $b_{ji,0}$ is multiplication, $b_{ji,1}=b_{ji}$, and the negative maps commute with evaluation.

Whenever the $T_{i,m}$ preserve the integral constructible subcategories [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], these comparisons restrict there and induce the same equations after scalar rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. The associators $a$ and the unit comparisons obey the pentagon and both unit laws. Their rationalizations are the canonical scalar-extension associator and units [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition]. Replacing each identity coefficient transition by the identity functor using its unit comparison gives a normalized scalar diagram (identity transitions and associators with repeated adjacent fields are identities). For a repeated coefficient field the line comparison still contains the prescribed signed-power map $b_{ji,m}$; after also identifying the signed lines along $b_{ji,m}$, the rationalized $\beta$ has identity components at repeated fields. With these line identifications the displayed tower and evaluation equations hold in the normalized diagram.

proof.text: Write $r_{ji}:R_i\to R_j$ for the ordinary coefficient-ring maps. Put $M_i=L_i^{[m]}$. In a trivialization $L_i=R_i e_i$, the positive power has basis $e_i^{\otimes m}$, the zero power has basis $1$, and the negative power has the dual basis; hence every $M_i$ is a line. Apply the tensor-power and dual scalar comparisons to $b_{ji}$ to obtain $b_{ji,m}:M_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\cong M_j$. For $m<0$ its formula is characterized by $b_{ji,-r}(f\otimes s)(b_{ji,r}(l\otimes t))=str_{ji}(f(l))$ for $r>0$. Thus it commutes with evaluation. The iteration and unitor clauses of the cited scalar comparison give $b_{20,m}=b_{21,m}(b_{10,m}\otimes1)$ and multiplication for $b_{ii,m}$. This includes $m=0$ and agrees with the specified $b_{ji}$ at $m=1$.

source.place: Tags 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback) and 03EO (lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor); signed-power evaluation formula is the agent expansion of blueprint Proof (3).

proof.text: The line-derived-tensor lemma, applied to $M_i$ and its dual, identifies $T_{i,m}$ with termwise tensor on arbitrary unbounded complexes and supplies its exact inverse and the specified evaluation. Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to K$. The complex $P\otimes M_i$ is again flat-term K-flat: its terms are flat since tensor by $M_i$ is an exact equivalence, and for acyclic $A$ the complex $A\otimes(P\otimes M_i)\cong(A\otimes P)\otimes M_i$ is acyclic. Change of rings preserves the flat-term K-flat class. The balanced map $((p\otimes l)\otimes s)\mapsto(p\otimes s)\otimes b_{ji,m}(l\otimes1)$ is consequently a chain isomorphism computing $B_{ji}T_{i,m}\cong T_{j,m}B_{ji}$. Its inverse is the reverse tensor reassociation followed by $b_{ji,m}^{-1}$. These are maps of sheafified tensors by their bilinear universal property. They are natural in chain maps, commute with differentials (the line is in degree zero), and hence with the inverted quasi-isomorphisms. The K-flat localization equivalence therefore descends them to the asserted natural isomorphism $\bar\beta_{ji,m}$ on $D(R_i)$. Lean realization of exact: the already specified sheaf evaluations at m and -m give an equivalence by CategoryTheory.Equivalence.mk. Equivalences preserve finite limits and colimits, and finite-colimit preservation implies additivity. This avoids repeating the local rank-one argument for exactness; the later representative arguments remain as above.

source.place: Tags 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change) and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), with the displayed representative map written out.

proof.text: Write $d_K:B_{21}B_{10}K\cong B_{20}K$ for the normalized ordinary scalar associator. Its formula is $(p\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto p\otimesr_{21}(s)t$. For the ordinary tower square, both paths on $((p\otimes l)\otimes s)\otimes t$ give $(p\otimesr_{21}(s)t)\otimes b_{20,m}(l\otimes1)$: step 1 gives exactly the equality of the two line factors. The ordinary evaluation square is checked on $((p\otimes l)\otimes f)\otimes s$ with $f\in M_i^\vee$; both paths give $p\otimesr_{ji}(f(l))s$. Evaluation is linear, so these computations hold after adding arbitrary scalars. Equality on the presheaf pure tensors implies equality after sheafification; the localization equivalence in step 2 then implies equality of the derived natural transformations. Thus the two displayed identities of the item hold with $B,d,\bar\beta$ replacing $C,a,\beta$. The unit square is the same calculation $((p\otimes l)\otimes s)\mapsto sp\otimes l$ when the ring map is the identity.

source.place: Tensor product section, before Tag 0GMW: scalar base-change and associativity identities; local evaluation calculation from blueprint Proof (3).

proof.text: Let $K$ be complete and write $K_n$ for its restricted derived reductions. The completeness definition supplies a distinguished triangle $K\to\prod_n^D K_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_n^D K_n\to K[1]$ with its prescribed quotient components. By the line-derived-tensor lemma, $T_{i,m}$ is a triangulated equivalence, and the equivalence-preserves-limits lemma identifies $T_{i,m}(\prod_n^D K_n)$ with $\prod_n^D T_{i,m}K_n$. The product existence and termwise representation hold by exact countable products and the derived-product theorem. The balanced chain formula $(p\otimes l)\otimes\bar a\mapsto(p\otimes\bar a)\otimes l$ identifies the reduction tower of $T_{i,m}K$ with $(T_{i,m}K_n)_n$, including transitions and quotient maps. Under these identifications the image triangle has first map the quotient components and second map $1-s$: project to its $n$th factor to get $q_n-t_nq_{n+1}$. It is therefore the required completeness triangle for $T_{i,m}K$.

source.place: Definition 3.5.2 and Proposition 3.5.1, p. 24: reduction-tower completeness; preservation by the line equivalence is the agent argument.

proof.text: The finite-free completed-scalar comparison supplies natural $\chi_{ji}:B_{ji}\to C_{ji}$, invertible on complete inputs, and says that $B_{ji}K$ is complete for complete $K$. Consequently $C_{ji}K$ is complete as well. Step 4 makes $\chi_{ji,T_{i,m}K}$ invertible. Define $\beta_{ji,m,K}=T_{j,m}(\chi_{ji,K})\bar\beta_{ji,m,K}\chi_{ji,T_{i,m}K}^{-1}$. All three factors are invertible and natural on complete inputs, giving the asserted natural isomorphism with no choice of an inverse at chain level. For later calculations put $z_K=\chi_{21,C_{10}K}\,B_{21}(\chi_{10,K}):B_{21}B_{10}K\cong C_{21}C_{10}K$. The transported associator is precisely $a_K=\chi_{20,K}d_Kz_K^{-1}$. All components in $z$ are invertible by completeness just established. In this and the following steps juxtaposition means composition, with the rightmost map applied first. Lean realization of extension_complete: keep the same K-flat resolution and reduction tower, compose its representative isomorphism with chi, and postcompose the connecting map with the shifted chi. A triangle isomorphism, identity on both products, transports distinguishedness and preserves the canonical augmentation legs.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, Lemma 3.4.12 and Proposition 3.5.1: prescribed completion comparisons; the conjugation is the agent construction.

proof.text: These formulas use the prescribed cone, rather than an arbitrary realization of a derived limit. On $P$ the comparison $\chi$ has product coordinates $p\otimes s\mapsto p\otimes\bar s$ and zero shifted-product coordinate, by the finite-free comparison statement. Applying the ordinary line map before the $n$th quotient gives $(p\otimes l)\otimes s\mapsto(p\otimes\bar s)\otimes b_{ji,m}(l\otimes1)$. The formula commutes with quotient transitions, since replacing $\bar s$ by its further reduction changes only that scalar. Thus step 5 is exactly conjugation by these specified quotient-cone maps. No inference that maps in the derived category are detected by finite projections, and no inverse chain map to $\chi$, is needed.

source.place: Definition 3.5.2, p. 24, with the strict cone and zero-component normalization specified in the cited nodes.

proof.text: For the completed tower equation precompose both sides by $z_{T_{0,m}K}$. In the left side substitute $a\,z=\chi_{20}d$ and $\beta\,\chi_T=T\chi\,\bar\beta$. Naturality of $\chi_{21}$ at $\beta_{10,m,K}$ and then naturality of $\bar\beta_{21,m}$ at $\chi_{10,K}$ move the inner comparisons next to their inverses. Cancelling them leaves $T_{2,m}(\chi_{20,K})\,T_{2,m}(d_K)\,\bar\beta_{21,m,B_{10}K}\,B_{21}(\bar\beta_{10,m,K})$. The right side becomes $T_{2,m}(\chi_{20,K})\,\bar\beta_{20,m,K}\,d_{T_{0,m}K}$. These agree by the ordinary tower equation in step 3. Since $z_{T_{0,m}K}$ is invertible, the completed equation follows.

source.place: Proof (3), final sentence; explicit natural-isomorphism cancellation for the coefficient-line tower.

proof.text: For the completed evaluation equation precompose by $\chi_{ji,T_{i,-m}T_{i,m}K}$. Two applications of $\beta\,\chi_T=T\chi\,\bar\beta$ turn the left side into $\epsilon_{j,m,C_{ji}K}\,T_{j,-m}T_{j,m}(\chi_{ji,K})\,T_{j,-m}(\bar\beta_{ji,m,K})\,\bar\beta_{ji,-m,T_{i,m}K}$. Naturality of evaluation moves $\chi$ to the outside. The ordinary evaluation equality of step 3 makes this $\chi_{ji,K}\,B_{ji}(\epsilon_{i,m,K})$. Naturality of $\chi_{ji}$ identifies it with $C_{ji}(\epsilon_{i,m,K})\,\chi_{ji,T_{i,-m}T_{i,m}K}$, the precomposed right side. The precomposing map is invertible by step 4, so it cancels. This proves exactly the order of twists in the displayed evaluation formula, including $m<0$ and $m=0$.

source.place: Proof (3), evaluation and inverse tensor pair; explicit naturality calculation after completion.

proof.text: The normalized ordinary associators have coherent iteration by the successive-extension lemma. For any four-field chain indexed $0,1,2,3$, with the same notation for its coefficient maps, their pentagon can also be read on $(((p\otimes s)\otimes t)\otimes u)$: either route gives $p\otimesr_{31}(s)r_{32}(t)u$. Their multiplication units obey both unit laws by $s\cdot1=s=1\cdot s$. For any longer coefficient chain identify its ordinary composite with its completed composite by successive $\chi$'s; for three arrows this identification is $\chi_{32,C_{21}C_{10}K}\,B_{32}(\chi_{21,C_{10}K})\,B_{32}B_{21}(\chi_{10,K})$. Naturality cancels the intermediate comparisons at every edge of the completed pentagon, leaving the ordinary pentagon. Thus it commutes. If $\lambda_i:B_{ii}\cong1$ is multiplication, the completed unit is $u_{i,K}=\lambda_{i,K}\chi_{ii,K}^{-1}$. The same cancellation converts both completed unit laws to the ordinary laws. The finite-free comparison identifies $u_i^{-1}$ with the specified natural completeness map, so these are the required units even when uniformizers for repeated fields differ. Lean realization of unit_normalization substitutes the normalized ordinary unit into the identity clause of finiteFreeCompletedScalarComparison; naturality is cancellation against chi. The repeated equality unfolds beta and unit and cancels inverse chi factors using functoriality.

source.place: Tensor product section, associativity and scalar base change; finite-free completion comparison for the repeated-field normalization.

proof.text: Assume now the stated preservation of the integral constructible subcategories by $T_{i,m}$. Integral scalar extension preserves them by the cited constructibility theorem. Thus every object and component above lies in those full subcategories, so their equations restrict without alteration. The transformations are coefficient-linear: their chain formulas are linear over the target coefficient sheaf and all factors of $\chi$ are morphisms in its module-derived category. Under rationalization each equation is sent to the same equation, since the localization sends composition to composition. On a morphism $\sum_r f_r\otimes a_r$ naturality is the sum of the integral naturality equations tensored by $a_r$ in the final field. Inverses remain inverses. The scalar associator and units just constructed are the ordinary tensor associator and multiplication transported by the specified completion comparison; their rationalizations are therefore the canonical scalar-extension comparisons of the cited scalar-composition theorem, using the integral-representative scalar functors in the rationalization definition. For intrinsic_complete, choose a prime different from l and the finite field ZMod q with its algebraic closure, then apply sfDerivedComplete_iff_legacy to the intrinsic completeness component. Full-subcategory isoMk restricts evaluation and beta. For rationalEpsilon and rationalBeta, localize each integral component, conjugate by the specified object equalities, prove naturality by tensor induction, and use the integral representatives for uniqueness. The rational evaluation and tower equalities are the localized integral equalities, transported with those component formulas and the scalar extension formula on 1 tensor f. The repeated-field rational equality follows similarly, including the inverses of the specified scalar-unit components. These Lean deductions use the still-stated ambient coherence assertions; they do not assert those holes closed.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10 and Proposition 3.5.1, together with the rationalization and scalar-composition constructions in the DAG; agent expansion of blueprint Proof (3).

proof.text: Finally replace repeated coefficient transitions by the identity using the specified completed unit and the ordinary multiplication unitor. Substituting the conjugation formula for beta identifies its scalar-normalized component with the ordinary signed-power comparison induced by b. It need not be identity for an arbitrary prescribed b. Identify the source and target signed lines along that comparison as well; the component then is identity. For the diagonal multiplication datum b_ii this line comparison is already the identity by the ordinary pure-tensor unit square. The two scalar unit laws make associators with repeated adjacent fields identity after scalar normalization. Transporting the tower and evaluation equations along both scalar and line identifications preserves them, and rationalization preserves the transported equations. This is the normalized diagram; no strict equality of the original completion functor with the identity is used.

statement_change.old_statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a scheme $X$, and a chain $E_0\subseteq E_1\subseteq E_2$ of finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, allowing repeated fields. For $i=0,1,2$ let $\mathcal O_i$ be the valuation ring, $\pi_i$ a uniformizer, and $R_i=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{i,X}$ the completed coefficient sheaf on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived completeness [def-weil-derived-complete]. For $i\leq j$, let $B_{ji}K=K\otimes^L_{R_i}R_j$ be ordinary derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], let $C_{ji}$ be the strict quotient-tower integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Explicitly, set $A_{i,n}=\mathcal O_i/\pi_i^n$ for $n\geq1$, and let $\rho_{ji,n}:R_i\to(A_{j,n})_X$ be the projection $R_i\to(A_{i,n})_X$ followed by the same-index quotient map induced by $\mathcal O_i\subseteq\mathcal O_j$. For a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex], put $Q_{ji,n}=\operatorname{Res}^{j}_n(P\otimes_{R_i}(A_{j,n})_X)$, where $\operatorname{Res}^{j}_n$ is restriction along $R_j\to(A_{j,n})_X$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Then $C_{ji}K$ is the specified complex
$$\operatorname{Cone}\left(1-s:\prod_{n\geq1}Q_{ji,n}\longrightarrow\prod_{n\geq1}Q_{ji,n}\right)[-1],\qquad s((q_n)_n)=(t_n(q_{n+1}))_n,$$
with termwise products and transitions $t_n$ induced by the quotient maps. Use its specified natural completion comparison $\chi_{ji}:B_{ji}\to C_{ji}$ [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison].

Let $L_i$ be a locally free rank-one $R_i$-module sheaf (locally isomorphic to $R_i$). Suppose given isomorphisms $b_{ji}:L_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\xrightarrow{\sim}L_j$ for $i\leq j$, with $b_{ii}$ the multiplication map and $b_{20}=b_{21}\circ(b_{10}\otimes1)$ under tensor associativity. Write $L_i^{[0]}=R_i$, $L_i^{[m]}=L_i^{\otimes m}$ for $m>0$, and $L_i^{[m]}=\mathcal Hom_{R_i}(L_i^{[-m]},R_i)$ for $m<0$, using [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Set $T_{i,m}K=K\otimes^L_{R_i}L_i^{[m]}$. The evaluation isomorphisms give $\epsilon_{i,m}:T_{i,-m}T_{i,m}\xrightarrow{\sim}1$.

For every integer $m$, the ordinary scalar comparisons induced from $b_{ji}$, its tensor powers and its sheaf-dual maps give natural isomorphisms $\bar\beta_{ji,m}:B_{ji}T_{i,m}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{j,m}B_{ji}$. Each $T_{i,m}$ preserves derived completeness. On complete inputs, the conjugated maps
$$\beta_{ji,m,K}=T_{j,m}(\chi_{ji,K})\circ\bar\beta_{ji,m,K}\circ\chi_{ji,T_{i,m}K}^{-1}$$
are natural isomorphisms $C_{ji}T_{i,m}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{j,m}C_{ji}$. Let $a_K:C_{21}C_{10}K\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{20}K$ be ordinary tensor associativity transported by these specified $\chi$ maps. They satisfy
$$T_{2,m}(a_K)\circ\beta_{21,m,C_{10}K}\circ C_{21}(\beta_{10,m,K})=\beta_{20,m,K}\circ a_{T_{0,m}K},$$
and
$$\epsilon_{j,m,C_{ji}K}\circ T_{j,-m}(\beta_{ji,m,K})\circ\beta_{ji,-m,T_{i,m}K}=C_{ji}(\epsilon_{i,m,K}).$$
For a repeated field the comparison is the one induced by the tensor unitor and the natural completeness map $K\to C_{ii}K$, rather than a strict equality $C_{ii}=1$. These are the comparisons for the prescribed quotient-tower completion: on a K-flat representative with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex], followed by each finite quotient projection, the ordinary map is $(x\otimes l)\otimes s\mapsto(x\otimes s)\otimes b_{ji,m}(l\otimes1)$. The maps $\chi$ in this conjugation are the quotient maps into the strict completion cone with zero shifted-product component; no chain-level inverse to $\chi$ is asserted. Here $b_{ji,m}$ is the signed-power extension of $b_{ji}$, so $b_{ji,0}$ is multiplication, $b_{ji,1}=b_{ji}$, and the negative maps commute with evaluation.

Whenever the $T_{i,m}$ preserve the integral constructible subcategories [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], these comparisons restrict there and induce the same equations after scalar rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. The associators $a$ and the unit comparisons obey the pentagon and both unit laws. Their rationalizations are the canonical scalar-extension associator and units [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition]. Replacing each identity transition by the identity functor using its unit comparison gives a normalized diagram (identity transitions and associators with repeated adjacent fields are identities); the rationalized $\beta$ then has identity components at repeated fields and satisfies the displayed tower and evaluation equations for that diagram.
statement_change.what: The original final sentence claims identity components after scalar-unit normalization for arbitrary compatible line isomorphisms at repeated fields. This is false: take X a nonempty geometric point, all coefficient fields Q_l, all lines equal to the coefficient unit, b10=-id, b21=id, b20=-id, and each diagonal bii the multiplication map. All the required integral line isomorphisms and cocycle equations hold, since -1 is a unit for every l. At m=1 and the unit object, scalar-normalized rational beta10 is -id, which differs from id in characteristic zero. Scalar normalization must retain the prescribed signed-power line map; identifying the lines along that map as well makes the normalized component identity. This is the canonical line transport used by blueprint Proof (3). The final proof step is corrected for the same reason.

old_proof.text: Write $r_{ji}:R_i\to R_j$ for the ordinary coefficient-ring maps. Put $M_i=L_i^{[m]}$. In a trivialization $L_i=R_i e_i$, the positive power has basis $e_i^{\otimes m}$, the zero power has basis $1$, and the negative power has the dual basis; hence every $M_i$ is a line. Apply the tensor-power and dual scalar comparisons to $b_{ji}$ to obtain $b_{ji,m}:M_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\cong M_j$. For $m<0$ its formula is characterized by $b_{ji,-r}(f\otimes s)(b_{ji,r}(l\otimes t))=str_{ji}(f(l))$ for $r>0$. Thus it commutes with evaluation. The iteration and unitor clauses of the cited scalar comparison give $b_{20,m}=b_{21,m}(b_{10,m}\otimes1)$ and multiplication for $b_{ii,m}$. This includes $m=0$ and agrees with the specified $b_{ji}$ at $m=1$.

source.place: Tags 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback) and 03EO (lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor); signed-power evaluation formula is the agent expansion of blueprint Proof (3).

old_proof.text: The line-derived-tensor lemma, applied to $M_i$ and its dual, identifies $T_{i,m}$ with termwise tensor on arbitrary unbounded complexes and supplies its exact inverse and the specified evaluation. Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to K$. The complex $P\otimes M_i$ is again flat-term K-flat: its terms are flat since tensor by $M_i$ is an exact equivalence, and for acyclic $A$ the complex $A\otimes(P\otimes M_i)\cong(A\otimes P)\otimes M_i$ is acyclic. Change of rings preserves the flat-term K-flat class. The balanced map $((p\otimes l)\otimes s)\mapsto(p\otimes s)\otimes b_{ji,m}(l\otimes1)$ is consequently a chain isomorphism computing $B_{ji}T_{i,m}\cong T_{j,m}B_{ji}$. Its inverse is the reverse tensor reassociation followed by $b_{ji,m}^{-1}$. These are maps of sheafified tensors by their bilinear universal property. They are natural in chain maps, commute with differentials (the line is in degree zero), and hence with the inverted quasi-isomorphisms. The K-flat localization equivalence therefore descends them to the asserted natural isomorphism $\bar\beta_{ji,m}$ on $D(R_i)$.

source.place: Tags 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change) and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), with the displayed representative map written out.

old_proof.text: Write $d_K:B_{21}B_{10}K\cong B_{20}K$ for the normalized ordinary scalar associator. Its formula is $(p\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto p\otimesr_{21}(s)t$. For the ordinary tower square, both paths on $((p\otimes l)\otimes s)\otimes t$ give $(p\otimesr_{21}(s)t)\otimes b_{20,m}(l\otimes1)$: step 1 gives exactly the equality of the two line factors. The ordinary evaluation square is checked on $((p\otimes l)\otimes f)\otimes s$ with $f\in M_i^\vee$; both paths give $p\otimesr_{ji}(f(l))s$. Evaluation is linear, so these computations hold after adding arbitrary scalars. Equality on the presheaf pure tensors implies equality after sheafification; the localization equivalence in step 2 then implies equality of the derived natural transformations. Thus the two displayed identities of the item hold with $B,d,\bar\beta$ replacing $C,a,\beta$. The unit square is the same calculation $((p\otimes l)\otimes s)\mapsto sp\otimes l$ when the ring map is the identity.

source.place: Tensor product section, before Tag 0GMW: scalar base-change and associativity identities; local evaluation calculation from blueprint Proof (3).

old_proof.text: Let $K$ be complete and write $K_n$ for its restricted derived reductions. The completeness definition supplies a distinguished triangle $K\to\prod_n^D K_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_n^D K_n\to K[1]$ with its prescribed quotient components. By the line-derived-tensor lemma, $T_{i,m}$ is a triangulated equivalence, and the equivalence-preserves-limits lemma identifies $T_{i,m}(\prod_n^D K_n)$ with $\prod_n^D T_{i,m}K_n$. The product existence and termwise representation hold by exact countable products and the derived-product theorem. The balanced chain formula $(p\otimes l)\otimes\bar a\mapsto(p\otimes\bar a)\otimes l$ identifies the reduction tower of $T_{i,m}K$ with $(T_{i,m}K_n)_n$, including transitions and quotient maps. Under these identifications the image triangle has first map the quotient components and second map $1-s$: project to its $n$th factor to get $q_n-t_nq_{n+1}$. It is therefore the required completeness triangle for $T_{i,m}K$.

old_proof.text: The finite-free completed-scalar comparison supplies natural $\chi_{ji}:B_{ji}\to C_{ji}$, invertible on complete inputs, and says that $B_{ji}K$ is complete for complete $K$. Consequently $C_{ji}K$ is complete as well. Step 4 makes $\chi_{ji,T_{i,m}K}$ invertible. Define $\beta_{ji,m,K}=T_{j,m}(\chi_{ji,K})\bar\beta_{ji,m,K}\chi_{ji,T_{i,m}K}^{-1}$. All three factors are invertible and natural on complete inputs, giving the asserted natural isomorphism with no choice of an inverse at chain level. For later calculations put $z_K=\chi_{21,C_{10}K}\,B_{21}(\chi_{10,K}):B_{21}B_{10}K\cong C_{21}C_{10}K$. The transported associator is precisely $a_K=\chi_{20,K}d_Kz_K^{-1}$. All components in $z$ are invertible by completeness just established. In this and the following steps juxtaposition means composition, with the rightmost map applied first.

old_proof.text: These formulas use the prescribed cone, rather than an arbitrary realization of a derived limit. On $P$ the comparison $\chi$ has product coordinates $p\otimes s\mapsto p\otimes\bar s$ and zero shifted-product coordinate, by the finite-free comparison statement. Applying the ordinary line map before the $n$th quotient gives $(p\otimes l)\otimes s\mapsto(p\otimes\bar s)\otimes b_{ji,m}(l\otimes1)$. The formula commutes with quotient transitions, since replacing $\bar s$ by its further reduction changes only that scalar. Thus step 5 is exactly conjugation by these specified quotient-cone maps. No inference that maps in the derived category are detected by finite projections, and no inverse chain map to $\chi$, is needed.

old_proof.text: For the completed tower equation precompose both sides by $z_{T_{0,m}K}$. In the left side substitute $a\,z=\chi_{20}d$ and $\beta\,\chi_T=T\chi\,\bar\beta$. Naturality of $\chi_{21}$ at $\beta_{10,m,K}$ and then naturality of $\bar\beta_{21,m}$ at $\chi_{10,K}$ move the inner comparisons next to their inverses. Cancelling them leaves $T_{2,m}(\chi_{20,K})\,T_{2,m}(d_K)\,\bar\beta_{21,m,B_{10}K}\,B_{21}(\bar\beta_{10,m,K})$. The right side becomes $T_{2,m}(\chi_{20,K})\,\bar\beta_{20,m,K}\,d_{T_{0,m}K}$. These agree by the ordinary tower equation in step 3. Since $z_{T_{0,m}K}$ is invertible, the completed equation follows.

old_proof.text: For the completed evaluation equation precompose by $\chi_{ji,T_{i,-m}T_{i,m}K}$. Two applications of $\beta\,\chi_T=T\chi\,\bar\beta$ turn the left side into $\epsilon_{j,m,C_{ji}K}\,T_{j,-m}T_{j,m}(\chi_{ji,K})\,T_{j,-m}(\bar\beta_{ji,m,K})\,\bar\beta_{ji,-m,T_{i,m}K}$. Naturality of evaluation moves $\chi$ to the outside. The ordinary evaluation equality of step 3 makes this $\chi_{ji,K}\,B_{ji}(\epsilon_{i,m,K})$. Naturality of $\chi_{ji}$ identifies it with $C_{ji}(\epsilon_{i,m,K})\,\chi_{ji,T_{i,-m}T_{i,m}K}$, the precomposed right side. The precomposing map is invertible by step 4, so it cancels. This proves exactly the order of twists in the displayed evaluation formula, including $m<0$ and $m=0$.

source.place: Proof (3), evaluation and inverse tensor pair; explicit naturality calculation after completion.

old_proof.text: The normalized ordinary associators have coherent iteration by the successive-extension lemma. For any four-field chain indexed $0,1,2,3$, with the same notation for its coefficient maps, their pentagon can also be read on $(((p\otimes s)\otimes t)\otimes u)$: either route gives $p\otimesr_{31}(s)r_{32}(t)u$. Their multiplication units obey both unit laws by $s\cdot1=s=1\cdot s$. For any longer coefficient chain identify its ordinary composite with its completed composite by successive $\chi$'s; for three arrows this identification is $\chi_{32,C_{21}C_{10}K}\,B_{32}(\chi_{21,C_{10}K})\,B_{32}B_{21}(\chi_{10,K})$. Naturality cancels the intermediate comparisons at every edge of the completed pentagon, leaving the ordinary pentagon. Thus it commutes. If $\lambda_i:B_{ii}\cong1$ is multiplication, the completed unit is $u_{i,K}=\lambda_{i,K}\chi_{ii,K}^{-1}$. The same cancellation converts both completed unit laws to the ordinary laws. The finite-free comparison identifies $u_i^{-1}$ with the specified natural completeness map, so these are the required units even when uniformizers for repeated fields differ.

old_proof.text: Assume now the stated preservation of the integral constructible subcategories by $T_{i,m}$. Integral scalar extension preserves them by the cited constructibility theorem. Thus every object and component above lies in those full subcategories, so their equations restrict without alteration. The transformations are coefficient-linear: their chain formulas are linear over the target coefficient sheaf and all factors of $\chi$ are morphisms in its module-derived category. Under rationalization each equation is sent to the same equation, since the localization sends composition to composition. On a morphism $\sum_r f_r\otimes a_r$ naturality is the sum of the integral naturality equations tensored by $a_r$ in the final field. Inverses remain inverses. The scalar associator and units just constructed are the ordinary tensor associator and multiplication transported by the specified completion comparison; their rationalizations are therefore the canonical scalar-extension comparisons of the cited scalar-composition theorem, using the integral-representative scalar functors in the rationalization definition.

old_proof.text: Finally replace each repeated-field arrow by the identity using $u_i$, and each ordinary repeated-field arrow using $\lambda_i$. The ordinary unit square of step 3 and $u_i\chi_{ii}=\lambda_i$ give $T_{i,m}(u_{i,K})\,\beta_{ii,m,K}=u_{i,T_{i,m}K}$. Hence its component in the normalized diagram is the identity. The two unit laws of step 9 say that an associator with a repeated adjacent field becomes the identity in that diagram. Conjugating the tower and evaluation equations by these unit components preserves both equalities; applying rationalization preserves them again. This is the claimed normalized diagram, while the original completed identity-extension functor remains related to the identity by its specified unit isomorphism.
